newsitem.title: USA: EqualNet may have to file bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: EqualNet may have to file bankruptcy.

text.p: EqualNet Holding Corp said Monday that if its efforts to obtain additional capital were unsuccessful, it would seek an alliance with a partner, and if no such alliance were accomplished, the company might be required to seek protection under U.S. bankruptcy laws.

As a result of management's focus on resolving the liquidity issues, the company said, it plans to file a notice with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission advising that it will be unable to file its annual report on Form 10-K on a timely basis. It said it expects to make the filing on or before October 13.

EqualNet reported a fourth quarter, ended June 30, loss of $865,000, which resulted in a loss for the year of $8.4 million. It said results for both periods reflect the impact of customer attrition related to provisioning time and operating systems transition issues over the past nine months.
"We have experienced a reduction in provisioning time over the last two quarters, which has resulted in fewer customer cancellations," noted Zane Russell chief executive.
"As well, our transition back to an enhanced version of our original NetBase operating system is complete," (and) ... We have resumed agent order activity."

As a result, Russel said, "In the beginning of our first fiscal quarter we are retaining more of our current customers while also adding new customers and getting back to what made us successful to start with."

Russell continued, "We are also pursuing a number of other strategies to improve revenues and earnings, including a joint venture which will enhance our product line by offering specialty long-distance calling cards ... and transferring our smallest customers to a LEC billing system whereby monthly statements are billed by the local phone service operator.

EqualNet said its borrowing capacity under its credit facility continues to decline as a result of operating losses, a decline in the revenue base, and the exclusion of certain receivables from the criteria of eligible receivables.

At current levels of operations and with a declining borrowing base, the company said, it must seek additional capital and continued concessions from vendors while continuing to reduce expenses to bring them in line with current levels of revenues.

EqualNet said it is negotiating with potential investors to secure between $2.5 million and $3.5 million from a private placement of convertible preferred stock and lenders to increase availability under its revolving credit facility, amend certain financial covenants and waive certain defaults.
